why: The new E1 example succeeded at teaching the model to avoid cutting inside very short, tightly bound units (improving ≤3 and ≤5 bins, see en_us_1427), but the E2/E3 replacements caused the model to shift some cutpoints earlier in mid-length pieces (≤7–≤10), producing isolated preverbal/verb fragments and splitting multiword name/title/number packages (examples en_us_133, en_us_1108, en_us_248 show cuts moved so verbs or numeric/title tokens became standalone fragments).
lesson: Keep examples that discourage cuts inside small cohesive packages while ensuring new examples do not incentivize earlier cuts that isolate verb/predicate cores or split multiword names/titles/numbers.
